atoms.name: mod
atoms.rule: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: neg
atoms.rule: - a is the negation of a.
atoms.plain: - a is the negation of a.

atoms.name: str_concat
atoms.rule: a v1_u2295_ b joins string a followed by string b.
atoms.plain: a v1_u2295_ b joins string a followed by string b.

atoms.name: str_length
atoms.rule: a v1_u2113_ is the number of characters in string a.
atoms.plain: a v1_u2113_ is the number of characters in string a.

atoms.name: str_reverse
atoms.rule: a v1_u21B6_ reverses the characters in string a.
atoms.plain: a v1_u21B6_ reverses the characters in string a.

atoms.name: str_first
atoms.rule: a v1_u2311_ is its first character, or the empty string when a is empty.
atoms.plain: a v1_u2311_ is its first character, or the empty string when a is empty.

atoms.name: str_drop
atoms.rule: a v1_u21E5_ removes its first character; the empty string stays empty.
atoms.plain: a v1_u21E5_ removes its first character; the empty string stays empty.

atoms.name: str_upper
atoms.rule: a v1_u21E7_ changes each lowercase letter in a to uppercase.
atoms.plain: a v1_u21E7_ changes each lowercase letter in a to uppercase.

atoms.name: str_lower
atoms.rule: a v1_u21E9_ changes each uppercase letter in a to lowercase.
atoms.plain: a v1_u21E9_ changes each uppercase letter in a to lowercase.

atoms.name: str_equal
atoms.rule: a ≡ b is true exactly when strings a and b have the same characters.
atoms.plain: a ≡ b is true exactly when strings a and b have the same characters.

domain.en: Values are strings and integers. Strings may be empty; integers count characters and steps.

settings.en: The preset that selects these atoms.
A recursive call repeats its step at most this many times; larger counts give NaN.
The largest number of cases in a branch definition.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: f1
operators.plain: Append b to a, then turn it into lowercase.

operators.name: f2
operators.definition: a f2 b = { (a f4 b) v1_u21E5_, if a ≡ "a"; a f4 b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals "a", apply f4 to a and b, then drop its first character; otherwise compute a f4 b.

operators.name: f3
operators.definition: a f3 b = { a, if b == 0; (a f3 (b - 1)) f29, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a f3 (b + 1)) f29, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): apply f29 to the current value.
